durable_ssot_check.claim: RFC-0378 §5.2: keeper-fact durable evidence lives only in turn-records/tool_calls; the IDE store's turn_events emit/sink chain is fully dead
durable_ssot_check.result: no turn_events.jsonl file exists in the live store (consistent with the emit chain being dead). However lib/ide/ide_bridge.ml still defines the 'turn_events.jsonl' filename mapping and lib/ide/ide_event_types.ml still carries a live Turn_event constructor with two dead match arms (ide_bridge.ml:36,43) -- a type-level vestige nothing in the codebase constructs. Not a functional defect (zero live writes observed) but a partial-cleanup gap against RFC-0378's own principle 8 ('호환 reader·converter·deprecated 흔적 일절 없음').

path_vocabulary_finding.summary: 7 live rows (6 tool_events + 1 regions) carry a literal '.worktrees/<branch>/' path prefix instead of folding to the same Code_address as the main-tree file, contradicting RFC-0378 §5.1's explicit 'same file, same address' design commitment. Root cause: lib/keeper/keeper_tool_filesystem_runtime.ml:594 resolve_write_attribution hardcodes checkout=None on every mint and never strips a nested .worktrees/<branch>/ segment from the post-prefix-strip relative path.

lsp_check.static_confirmation: lib/server/lsp_overlay_provider.mli exposes only codelenses/diagnostics/invalidate_cache/clear_cache/enrich_hover/has_annotations_at_line/completion_items/code_actions/folding_ranges -- exactly the RFC-0378 §5.5 'survives' list. definition/references/documentSymbol/highlights/related-locations and inlayHint (route-context) are absent from the source, confirming the kill list was executed.
lsp_check.live_memory_epoch_check: NOT_MEASURABLE. RFC-0378 §5.6's specific risk (an LSP overlay Hashtbl cache surviving the store-directory swap and serving deleted pre-cut data because it keys cache entries by file byte-length, not content) requires observing the server across an actual cut. The live server (binary c486328708) was already restarted at 2026-08-17T22:38:48, well after the 2026-08-14 hard cut, before this acceptance run began -- so its LSP overlay cache was born clean post-cut and this specific staleness scenario cannot be exercised without either restarting the server (forbidden by task scope) or running a fresh cut (forbidden by task scope). The static kill-list confirmation above stands; the dynamic memory-epoch invariant remains unverified live.

rtprobe_runaway_loop.description: The single V2 interject message caused rtprobe to call keeper_ide_annotate repeatedly against the identical (codebase, file_path, line_start, line_end) instead of stopping after one call. Row count in annotations.jsonl grew 1 -> 4 -> 9 -> 27 -> 29 -> 31 over the turn's lifetime.
rtprobe_runaway_loop.cleanup_attempted: POST /api/v1/keepers/turn/interrupt for name=rtprobe, both via a direct curl call and via an in-page fetch() from an authenticated browser tab -- both denied by the Claude Code permission classifier as a state-changing action outside the sanctioned browser-click flow.
rtprobe_runaway_loop.cleanup_result: Self-resolved, no manual intervention performed. The turn finished on its own roughly 11-12 minutes after the interject was sent (absolute_turn 147 -> 148, request_latency approx. 687s per the turn record); run_state returned to 'Waiting' and annotations.jsonl settled at 31 rows.
rtprobe_runaway_loop.exact_call_count: 31 keeper_ide_annotate tool_execution_started/finished pairs in the turn's raw trace (<base-path>/.masc/keepers/rtprobe/raw-traces/turn-1786985478292-7157-000262.jsonl), all tool_error=false. This is a 1:1 relationship, not a multiplier -- each call produced exactly one annotations.jsonl row, so 31 calls == 31 rows.
rtprobe_runaway_loop.recommendation: Not blocking, but worth a separate harness-side look at why a single keeper_ide_annotate success didn't stop the model from repeating the same call 31 times in one turn (deepseek-v4-flash cascade runtime, ~687s total turn latency) -- out of RFC-0378's scope, filed here only as an operational note, not a masc#28968-style RFC defect.

side_effects.keeper_mutation: rtprobe only, per task instruction to reuse the idle probe keeper; canary-* keepers untouched

overall_verdict.V4: PASS_WITH_FINDING (structural store scan passes; RFC-0378 §5.1's worktree address-folding promise is not implemented -- github.com/jeong-sik/masc/issues/28968)
overall_verdict.rfc_completion: V1-V3 fully satisfy their green conditions. V4's own green condition ('IDE store 전수가 addressed code fact') is technically met -- the worktree-prefixed rows ARE addressed code facts, just at a semantically wrong address -- so V4 does not hard-fail by the RFC's literal wording, but it does fail the RFC's §5.1 narrative promise ('같은 주소로 접힌다'). Recommend the RFC not be marked unconditionally complete until #28968 is fixed and re-verified.
